measures.title: Proposition 1
measures.summary: Issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund Multifamily Housing Program, CalVet Home Loan Program, and youth housing

measures.title: Proposition 2
measures.summary: Increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) cap from 10% of general fund revenue to 20% and excluding deposits into the BSA from the Gann Limit

measures.title: Proposition 3
measures.summary: Renew the additional income taxes enacted with the approval of Proposition 30 in 2012 that fund education and early childhood programs.

measures.title: Proposition 4
measures.summary: Allow the state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules

measures.title: Proposition 5
measures.summary: Eliminate the successor election when a state officer is recalled, thereby leaving the office vacant until it is filled according to state law

measures.title: Proposition 37
measures.summary: Establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for qualified homebuyers on qualifying homes and issue $25 billion in bonds to fund the program

measures.title: Proposition 38
measures.summary: Issue $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds to fund immunology and immunotherapy research

measures.title: Proposition 39
measures.summary: Require voters to present government-issued identification when casting ballots and require election officials to use government data to confirm voter citizenship and report verification rates

measures.title: Proposition 40
measures.summary: Levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth of taxpayers and trusts with covered assets valued over $1 billion to fund state health care programs, food assistance programs, and public education

measures.title: Proposition 41
measures.summary: Require state laws or ballot initiatives levying a new special tax enacted after January 1, 2026 to require the government entities or departments receiving revenue from the new tax to eliminate their lowest-performing programs and reinvest those savings in higher-performing programs

measures.title: Proposition 42
measures.summary: Prohibit the enactment of new taxes after January 1, 2026 on ownership or accumulation of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings

measures.title: Proposition 43
measures.summary: Require two-thirds vote by electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local governments and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes except those authorized elsewhere in the state constitution

measures.title: Proposition 44
measures.summary: Prohibit healthcare clinics, specifically federally-qualified health centers and related organizations, from spending less than 90% of their annual revenue on mission-related purposes

measures.title: Proposition 45
measures.summary: Establish timelines for local and state agencies to review plans and solicit public comment for essential projects, such as housing, improvements to water supply, transportation, energy, and facilities for health and public safety

measures.title: Proposition RTM
measures.summary: Create a sales tax for a 14-year period to fund transportation programs in the region

measures.title: Proposition A
measures.summary: Amend the San Francisco Charter to remove outdated provisions and make  changes to the governance of local programs and departments

measures.title: Proposition B
measures.summary: Amend the San Francisco Charter to create a municipal finance corporation and a public bank

measures.title: Proposition C
measures.summary: Change the method of annual contributions to the city's Housing Trust Fund

measures.title: Proposition D
measures.summary: Make changes to the city's ballot measure referral and initiative process

measures.title: Proposition E
measures.summary: Require the Board of Supervisors to approve all city contracts that would generate more than $4.5 million or cost more than $25 million and amend the city administrator's roles and authority

measures.title: Proposition F
measures.summary: Amend the structure of the executive branch of the city government and the authorities and duties of the mayor

measures.title: Proposition G
measures.summary: Open the Upper Great Highway to public vehicles on weekdays, except on holidays

measures.title: Proposition H
measures.summary: Implement a 15-year property tax to fund the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency

measures.title: Proposition J
measures.summary: Remove the real estate transfer tax exemption for transfers that occur due to a foreclosure

measures.title: Proposition I
measures.summary: Dedicate 50% of the revenue from the real estate transfer tax to housing and development purposes
